data.narrative:
Trilobio is a seed-stage biotech company founded by Roya Amini-Naieni and Maximilian Schommer that has raised $11M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 3 public biotech companies (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private-stage peers in Biotech & Health, though narrow peer comparables proved insufficient for median-based triangulation.

Stage-progression analysis, the sole applicable method, projects Trilobio's valuation by applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier from seed to next stage against the $11M raised proxy, yielding $28M. A sensitivity analysis incorporating ±15% variance around this central estimate produces a low bound of $23M and a high bound of $32M. Public biotech peers trade at a median P/S multiple of 7.4x across the three comparable tickers, but this anchor cannot be applied without Trilobio's revenue figures, which remain unavailable.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $23M to $32M, centered at $28M, contingent on the stage-progression framework. Key uncertainties include the applicability of the 2.5x multiplier to this specific company and sector—particularly given the absence of validated peer-median data—and the lack of revenue visibility needed to benchmark against public comparables. Further diligence on capital efficiency, clinical-stage risk, and actual fundraising terms would refine this range materially.
